newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Guerrillas planned big attacks in Colombia capital.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas planned big attacks in Colombia capital.

text.p: Colombian authorities have uncovered plans by leading leftist guerrilla group to unleash a series of high-profile attacks in the capital, Bogota, police sources said on Friday.
They said the plans by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels were discovered during recent police intelligence operations in Bogota and the northern cities of Bucaramnga and Cucuta.
Details were not immediately available, but a National Police spokesman told Reuters a rebel arsenal earmarked for the offensive in Bogota included 18 high-powered rockets.
The FARC's targets were to have included government offices and police and military installations across the capital, the spokesman added.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, launched a nationwide offensive in late August that military officials have described as Colombia's worst in more than three decades of war.
National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano and Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra scheduled a news conference for later on Friday to discuss the planned rebel offensive in the capital.
